# E-M10 Mark II code loaded from the card, fenykl loader

After one flash, the loader runs FENYKL.BIN, or a FENYKL.TST once, from the card on power-switch and battery-connect boots.

**Camera:** [Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II](../cameras/em10-ii.md) · **Project:** [fenykl](../projects/fenykl.md)

**Firmware:** [E-M10 Mark II firmware 1.4, build 1400](../firmware/em10-ii-1400.md) · **Mod build:** fenykl-loader with FENYKL.TST and battery-connect boots

With the fenykl loader on firmware 1.4, a power-switch boot, or a battery connected with the switch On, reads C:\FENYKL.TST once (deleting it first) or C:\FENYKL.BIN, checks its header, checksum and model and runs it as a CPU0 task; after fault resets the camera boots without the payload.

**Availability:** experimental branch. **Implementation basis:** reported.

## Supporting observations

- [E-M10 Mark II fenykl loader: maintainer's camera](../evidence/em10-ii-fenykl-loader-current.md) — physical camera; reported pass; partial report; release label only.

## Limits

- No release; users build the patched update file from the repository and a stock file they supply.
- Reported on the maintainer's camera; the hash of the flashed loader is not recorded, and refused invalid images are simulator-tested only.
- Cable, card-insertion and switch-Off boots run no payload by design, per the loader source; those boots are not covered by the linked report.
- A payload runs with full firmware rights and is not isolated; removing the card undoes nothing a payload saved to flash, EEPROM or settings.
- The OK-held card update runs before the loader, so reflashing stock from the card stays available; a PC update with the payload on the card must be avoided.
